public_rationale: The condition was met: ChatGPT went from 500 million weekly users at the end of March 2025 to about 700 million by August and 800 million by October (e1). The first part held. After GPT-5 launched in August 2025, Altman set out how OpenAI would ration compute and said current capacity could support only about 30% more API growth (e2). The second part, that OpenAI had little room to expand, did not hold. In the same August posts Altman said OpenAI was roughly doubling its compute fleet within five months (e4). In November 2025 OpenAI signed a $38B deal with AWS for hundreds of thousands of Nvidia GPUs (e3). So OpenAI did hit capacity limits, but it found substantial room to expand.
limitations: 'At this rate' is undefined. Growth slowed somewhat in absolute pace, though it stayed strong.

our_interpretation: Antecedent: OpenAI's user growth kept going strongly after March 2025 (500 million weekly users). Strong continued growth, not an exact match to the early-2025 pace, is taken as meeting it.
Outcome has two parts: (a) OpenAI later hits capacity problems such as rate limits or rationing compute; (b) OpenAI lacks room to add much more compute.
No deadline is stated, so the claim can be settled only by decisive dated events.
criteria.support_condition: After growth continued, OpenAI reported capacity shortfalls, and it could not secure much more compute.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After growth continued, OpenAI had no capacity problems, or it secured large new compute capacity showing ample room to expand.

evidence.excerpt: In August, OpenAI said it was on the cusp of reaching 700 million weekly active users, already an increase from 500 million weekly active users at the end of March.
evidence.explanation: User growth continued strongly after the post, from 500M to about 700M by August and 800M by October 2025, so the antecedent is met on a plain reading.

evidence.excerpt: We will then prioritize API demand up to the currently allocated capacity and commitments we've made to customers. (For a rough sense, we can support about an additional ~30% new API growth from where we are today with this capacity.)
evidence.explanation: After GPT-5's launch, OpenAI had to ration compute between user groups because of capacity limits, matching part (a).

evidence.excerpt: Under this new $38 billion agreement, which will have continued growth over the next seven years, OpenAI is accessing AWS compute comprising hundreds of thousands of state-of-the-art NVIDIA GPUs
evidence.explanation: OpenAI secured access to hundreds of thousands of new GPUs from a non-Microsoft provider, which contradicts part (b), 'not much room to expand'.

evidence.excerpt: We are ~doubling our compute fleet over the next 5 months (!) so this situation should get better.
evidence.explanation: OpenAI said it was about to roughly double its compute fleet, against the claim that it had little room to expand.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: A dated OpenAI statement of capacity shortfalls after continued growth settles part (a). Part (b) is separately settled against the claim by e3 (2025-11-03).
